This clause describes the lexical tokens used in Verilog HDL source text and their conventions. An introduction that states no rule; the rules are §3.1 to §3.8.2.

White space shall contain the characters for spaces, tabs, newlines, and formfeeds. These characters shall be ignored except when they serve to separate other lexical tokens. However, blanks and tabs shall be considered significant characters in strings Defines white space and where it counts; no form is illegal (a token split by white space is §3.1's, cited both ways). Positive: 03_lexical_conventions/b_3_2_white_space.v (tab, formfeed and newline separators; blanks and a raw tab stored in a string).

Real numbers shall be converted to integers by rounding the real number to the nearest integer, rather than by truncating it. ... The ties shall be rounded away from zero. A conversion rule; nothing is illegal. Positive: 03_lexical_conventions/b_3_5_3_real_to_integer_rounding.v (the clause's five values, ties on both sides of zero).

String variables are variables of reg type (see 4.2) with width equal to the number of characters in the string multiplied by 8. The width a string needs; nothing is illegal (a narrower or wider reg is §3.6.2's truncation and padding). Positive: 03_lexical_conventions/audit_lexical_packed_strings.v, 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_string_test.v.

Strings can be manipulated using the Verilog HDL operators. The value being manipulated by the operator is the sequence of 8-bit ASCII values. and the right-justify, zero-pad, left-truncate rule. Permissive; nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_string_test.v (the clause's string_test, which §5.2.3 repeats), 03_lexical_conventions/audit_lexical_packed_strings.v (padding and truncation).

Table 3-1's escapes \n \t \\ \" \ddd. "If less than three characters are used, the following character shall not be an octal digit." fixes how an escape is read (at most three octal digits) rather than forbidding a source; "Implementations may issue an error if the character represented is greater than \377" is optional. Positive: 03_lexical_conventions/audit_lexical_packed_strings.v (every escape; 1-, 2- and 3-digit octal).

Eight examples of attribute placement; §1.8: "These examples are informative." The rules are §3.8 and §3.8.2 (cited both ways). Positive: 03_lexical_conventions/b_3_8_1_examples.v (xfail: any attribute instance stops digital execution, E1100).
The set of Verilog HDL data types is designed to represent the data storage and transmission elements found in digital hardware. The chapter preamble; its rules are in §4.1 to §4.11.

The four values, z at a gate input or in an expression acting as x except through MOS switches, and "All bits of vectors can be independently set to one of the four basic values." Nothing is illegal. Positive: 04_data_types/b_4_1_value_set.v.

There are two main groups of data types: the variable data types and the net data types. These two groups differ in the way that they are assigned and hold values. They also represent different hardware structures. An introduction; the rules are §4.2.1 and §4.2.2, each cited both ways.

A net or reg declaration without a range specification shall be considered 1 bit wide and is known as a scalar. Multibit net and reg data types shall be declared by specifying a range. Nothing is illegal (the range rules are §4.3.1's). Positive: 04_data_types/b_4_3_scalar_and_vector.v.

column3: Ideal capacitive state and charge decay

column4: Rounding to nearest with ties away from zero, and x/z bits taken as zero when converting to real. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 04_data_types/b_4_8_2_real_integer_conversion.v, b_4_8_2_unknown_bits_to_real.v (xfail).

The symbols for the Verilog HDL operators are similar to those in the C programming language. Table 5-1 lists these operators. A list, no "shall"; the real-operand restrictions are §5.1.1 (cited both ways). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_every_operator.v (every Table 5-1 row).

Table 5-4 and "All operators shall associate left to right with the exception of the conditional operator, which shall associate right to left." Parsing rules that give every well-formed expression one reading; nothing is forbidden. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_2_precedence.v (15 groupings where the wrong reading differs, and one parenthesised).

An integer with no base specifier shall be interpreted as a signed value in twos-complement form. An integer with an unsigned base specifier shall be interpreted as an unsigned value. Interpretation rules; no form is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_3_integer_number_signedness.v (the clause's four IntA results).

However, if the final result of an expression can be determined early, the entire expression need not be evaluated. Whether a short-circuited operand is evaluated is left open, so no test may assert one outcome (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5); the first sentence defers to §5.1.2 (05_expressions/b_5_1_2_precedence.v).

Division truncation, x on a zero divisor, modulus sign, the power rules of Tables 5-6/5-8; the only open cases are "unspecified" (a zero base with a nonpositive exponent, or a negative base with a non-integral exponent, when an operand is real). Nothing is illegal (the real-operand ban on % is §5.1.1). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_5_division_modulus_power.v, audit_expr_arithmetic_unknowns.v.

column3: Arithmetic expressions with regs and integers
column4: A value assigned to a reg variable or a net shall be treated as an unsigned value unless ... declared to be signed. ... Conversions between signed and unsigned values shall keep the same bit representation Interpretation rules (Table 5-9); nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_6_reg_integer_interpretation.v (the clause's example and every Table 5-9 row but real).

Results, extension, real conversion and precedence of relational operators; relational operators are legal on every operand type (Table 5-2). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_7_relational_extension.v, audit_expr_arithmetic_unknowns.v.

Precedence, zero/sign extension, x results of == and != and exact matching of === and !==; the ban on === with real operands is §5.1.1 Table 5-3 (05_expressions/b_5_1_1_real_case_equality_rejected.v). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_8_equality_extension_and_unknowns.v.

Results (1, 0 or x), precedence and negation of the logical operators; logical operators are legal on every operand type, reals included (Table 5-2). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_9_logical_connectives.v, audit_expr_logical_unknowns.v.

the operator shall combine a bit in one operand with its corresponding bit in the other operand (Tables 5-12 to 5-16) and "the shorter operand is zero-filled in the most significant bit positions." Nothing is illegal (bitwise operators on reals are §5.1.1's ban). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_10_bitwise_tables.v (every cell of Tables 5-12 to 5-16).

The stepwise definition of reduction and/or/xor and their inversions; nothing is illegal (reduction of a real is §5.1.1's ban). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_11_reduction_steps.v (Table 5-20 and x/z steps), expressions.v.

Fill rules, x/z right operand, unsigned right operand, result signedness; nothing is illegal (shifting a real is §5.1.1's ban). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_12_shift_fill_and_sign.v (the clause's two examples and every stated rule).

Condition by == 0, Table 5-21 merging, the real-operand 0, zero-fill of the shorter operand, right associativity (§5.1.2); nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_1_13_conditional_ambiguous.v (includes the clause's busa example), b_5_1_2_precedence.v, expressions.v.

Lists the operand forms: whole name ("all of the bits ... shall be used"), bit-select, part-select, array element and its selects, concatenation, function call. The illegal selects are §5.2.1's and §5.2.2's, each cited both ways. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_operand_forms.v; b_5_2_2_element_selects.v (xfail: selects of an array element).

String operands shall be treated as constant numbers consisting of a sequence of 8-bit ASCII codes ... Any Verilog HDL operator can manipulate string operands. Permissive; nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_string_test.v (the clause's string_test), audit_expr_string_numeric_padding.v.

Copy is provided by simple assignment. Concatenation is provided by the concatenation operator. Comparison is provided by the equality operators. The 8*n width is a "should". Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_1_copy_concatenate_compare.v.

column3: String value padding and potential problems
column4: When strings are assigned to variables, the values stored shall be padded on the left with zeros. ... The comparison and concatenation operators shall not distinguish between zeros resulting from padding and the original string characters (\0, ASCII NUL). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_2_padding_breaks_compare.v (the clause's s1/s2 example).

The null string (") shall be considered equivalent to the ASCII NUL (\0"), which has a value zero (0), which is different from a string "0"." Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_2_3_3_null_string.v, audit_expr_string_numeric_padding.v.

column3: Minimum, typical, and maximum delay expressions
column4: Values expressed in min:typ:max format can be used in expressions. The min:typ:max format can be used wherever expressions can appear. Permissive; which of the three a tool selects is not fixed by the clause, so the positive fixture accepts any member. Positive: 05_expressions/audit_expr_mintypmax_context.v.

In the case of the addition operator, the bit length of the largest operand, including the left-hand side of an assignment, shall be used. A sizing rule; nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_4_sum_width_from_lhs.v (the clause's sumA/sumB example).

Table 5-22's bit lengths for every expression form; nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_4_1_table_5_22_widths.v (every row but the implementation-sized unsized constant), expressions.v, audit_expr_unsized_unknown_extension.v.

During the evaluation of an expression, interim results shall take the size of the largest operand (in case of an assignment, this also includes the left-hand side). Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_4_2_bitlength_example.v (both of the clause's examples, "answer = 01000"), expressions.v.
An example of the §5.4.1 rules: a*b, {a**b} and a**b under self- and context-determined sizing. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_4_3_self_determined_example.v (the clause's three values).

two system functions shall be used to handle type casting on expressions: $signed() and $unsigned(). These functions shall evaluate the input expression and return a value with the same size and value of the input expression and the type defined by the function. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_5_signed_unsigned_functions.v (the clause's regA/regB/regS example), audit_expr_signed_boundaries.v, audit_expr_cast_width.v.

The type rules (decimal signed, based unsigned unless s, selects/concatenations/comparisons unsigned, any unsigned operand makes the result unsigned, any real makes it real). Nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_5_1_expression_type_rules.v, audit_expr_signed_boundaries.v, audit_expr_unknown_extension.v.

Propagation of type and size to context-determined operands, the real and relational exceptions, and sign extension of primaries only under a signed type. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_5_2_real_and_relational_operands.v, expressions.v.

If needed, extend the size of the right-hand side, performing sign extension if, and only if, the type of the right-hand side is signed. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_5_3_assignment_extension.v, audit_expr_cast_width.v.

column3: Handling X and Z in signed expressions
column4: x/z fill of a resized signed value and "any nonlogical operation involving the value shall result in the entire resultant value being an X". Nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_5_4_signed_unknown_bits.v, audit_expr_unknown_extension.v.

the MSBs of the right-hand expression will always be discarded to match the size of the left-hand side. Implementations are not required to warn or report any errors related to assignment size mismatch or truncation. Truncation is legal by definition. Positive: 05_expressions/b_5_6_truncation_examples.v (the clause's three examples), audit_expr_truncation_direction.v.

There are 14 logic gates and 12 switches predefined in the Verilog HDL and two advantages of gate modeling; an overview that states no rule. The inventory is Table 7-1 (§7.1.1, cited both ways; 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_1_1_every_primitive.v instantiates all 26).

Strengths and values of combined signals
column4: a net shall have either a single unambiguous strength level or an ambiguous strength consisting of more than one level. When signals combine, their strengths and values shall determine the strength and value of the resulting signal in accordance with the principles in 7.10.1 through 7.10.4. A resolution rule; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_10_figure_combinations.v (Figures 7-4, 7-9, 7-16).

the stronger signal shall dominate all the weaker drivers and determine the result. The combination of two or more signals of like value shall result in the same value with the greater of all the strengths. Resolution; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_01_drive_strength_dominance.v, d03_14_wired_unequal_strength.v, b_7_9_strength_levels.v.

When two signals of equal strength and opposite value combine, the result shall be a value x and "The combination of two signals of ambiguous strength shall result in a signal of ambiguous strength." Resolution; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_10_figure_combinations.v, d03_13_wired_equal_strength_table.v, d03_15_wired_ambiguous_strength.v, audit_primitive_ambiguous_same_polarity.v.

column3: Ambiguous strength signals and unambiguous signals
column4: Rules a) to c): levels above the unambiguous signal remain, levels at or below it disappear, a gap between opposite values is filled. Resolution; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_04_ambiguous_strength_range.v, audit_primitive_ambiguous_same_polarity.v, d03_05_tri0_tri1_pull_strength.v, b_7_10_figure_combinations.v (PuH against St0 -> 0).

The net types triand, wand, trior, and wor shall resolve conflicts when multiple drivers have the same strength. Resolution; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_07_wired_logic_under_strength.v, d03_13_wired_equal_strength_table.v, d03_14_wired_unequal_strength.v, d03_15_wired_ambiguous_strength.v.

The nmos, pmos, and cmos switches shall pass the strength from the data input to the output, except that a supply strength shall be reduced to a strong strength. (and the same for tran, tranif0, tranif1). A propagation rule; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_11_supply_reduced_to_strong.v (supply through nmos, pmos, cmos, tran, tranif1 meets St0 -> x; pull passes unchanged), audit_switch_bits_strength_delay.v.

The rnmos, rpmos, rcmos, rtran, rtranif1, and rtranif0 devices shall reduce the strength of signals that pass through them according to Table 7-8. A propagation rule; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_12_resistive_reduction_table.v (supply->pull, pull->weak, weak->medium, highz->highz across all six devices), d08_strength_reduction.v, audit_switch_bits_strength_delay.v.

The tri0, tri1, supply0, and supply1 net types shall generate signals with specific strength levels. The trireg declaration can specify either of two signal strength levels other than a default strength level. Nothing is illegal here (the charge-strength form is §7.13.2, cited both ways). Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_05_tri0_tri1_pull_strength.v, d03_06_supply_net_strength.v.

In the absence of an overriding source, such a signal shall have a value 0 and a pull strength. (tri1: 1 and pull). Nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_05_tri0_tri1_pull_strength.v.
The supply0 and supply1 net types shall have supply driving strengths. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_06_supply_net_strength.v, b_7_11_supply_reduced_to_strong.v.

There shall be no required relation (e.g., min ≤ typ ≤ max) between the expressions for minimum, typical, and maximum delays. These can be any three expressions. Permissive; nothing is illegal. Positive: 05_expressions/audit_expr_mintypmax_context.v (3:2:1 accepted); 07_gate_switch_level/b_7_14_1_unordered_delay_triples.v (xfail: #(5:3:1) on a gate, net or assign does not parse).

The third delay shall specify the charge decay time instead of the delay in a transition to the z logic state. and "The z value shall not propagate from the drivers of a trireg net to a trireg net." Behaviour rules; nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_08_trireg_charge_decay.v, d03_09_trireg_capacitive_hold.v.

The decay "shall begin when the drivers of the trireg net turn off" and ends when the decay time elapses (1 or 0 -> x) or a driver turns on. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_08_trireg_charge_decay.v (both end conditions).

column3: Delay specification for charge decay time
column4: The third delay in a trireg net declaration shall specify the charge decay time. The decay is the third position of delay3, so no expressible source violates "preceded by a rise and a fall delay". Positive: 07_gate_switch_level/d03_08_trireg_charge_decay.v (#(0, 0, 50)).

In combinational UDPs, the output state is determined solely as a function of the current input states. ... "All combinations of the inputs that are not explicitly specified will drive the output state to the unknown value x." Evaluation rules; nothing is illegal (the table-shape bans are §8.1.4's, an edge in a combinational table is A.5.3's: 08_udp/d08_reject_udp_comb_edge.v). Positive: 08_udp/b_8_2_multiplexer.v (the clause's two tables over all 27 input combinations), audit_udp_comb_level.v, d08_udp_comb.v.

UDP definitions allow a mixing of the level-sensitive and the edge-sensitive constructs in the same table. When the input changes, the edge-sensitive cases are processed first, followed by level-sensitive cases. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 08_udp/b_8_7_jk_edge_ff.v (the clause's jk_edge_ff), audit_udp_potential_edges_dominance.v.

Table 8-3 and "When the edge-sensitive case is processed first, followed by the level-sensitive case, the output changes to 1." An explanation of §8.7's order; nothing is illegal. Positive: 08_udp/audit_udp_potential_edges_dominance.v (an edge row and a level row match one input change with different outputs and the level row wins); no input sequence reaches Table 8-3's own case (b_8_7_jk_edge_ff.v says why).
This clause starts with a brief overview of a behavioral model to provide a context for many types of behavioral statements in the Verilog HDL. The chapter preamble; its rules are in §9.1 to §9.9.2.

Verilog behavioral models contain procedural statements ... These constructs are formally described in 9.9. An overview; the rules are §9.9's. Its model `behave` is run by 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_9_initial_and_always.v.

column3: The assign and deassign procedural statements
The force and release procedural statements

column4: If the expression evaluates to true (that is, has a nonzero known value), the first statement shall be executed. If it evaluates to false (that is, has a zero value or the value is x or z), the first statement shall not execute. and the else binds to "the closest previous if that lacks an else". Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_4_if_truth_and_else_binding.v, control.v.

The expressions shall be evaluated in order. If any expression is true, the statement associated with it shall be executed, and this shall terminate the whole chain. The trailing else "can be omitted". Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_4_1_if_else_if_chain.v.

Do-not-care values (z values for casez, z and x values for casex) in any bit of either the case expression or the case items shall be treated as do-not-care conditions during the comparison. Matching rules; nothing is illegal (multiple defaults are §9.5's ban). Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_5_1_dont_care_examples.v (the clause's two examples), control.v.

A constant expression can be used for case expression. The value of the constant expression shall be compared against case item expressions. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_5_2_constant_case_expression.v (the clause's priority encoder).

The four loops; a repeat count or for condition that is x or z "shall be treated as zero", a while that "starts out false" never executes. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_6_loop_rules.v, control.v.
The Verilog HDL has two types of explicit timing control over when procedural statements can occur. An overview naming delay control, event control and wait, whose rules are §9.7.1 to §9.7.7.

If the delay expression evaluates to an unknown or high-impedance value, it shall be interpreted as zero delay. If the delay expression evaluates to a negative value, it shall be interpreted as a twos-complement unsigned integer of the same size as a time variable. Interpretation rules; nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_7_1_delay_values.v.

Table 9-1's posedge/negedge transitions, "An edge event shall be detected only on the least significant bit of the expression", and an operand change without a result change is no event. Nothing is illegal (an edge of a real is §4.8.1's ban). Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_7_2_edge_detection.v (all 12 transitions), b_9_7_2_expression_event.v (xfail).

The keyword or or a comma character (,) is used as an event logical or operator. A combination of these can be used in the same event expression. Comma-separated sensitivity lists shall be synonymous to or-separated sensitivity lists. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_7_4_event_or.v.

@* adds "all nets and variables that are read by the statement", with two stated exceptions and the inclusions listed. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/d04_01_implicit_sensitivity_star.v, d04_02_implicit_sensitivity_cascade.v, d04_16_implicit_sensitivity_paren_star.v, audit_sched_implicit_event_exclusion.v, audit_sched_implicit_lhs_index.v, audit_sched_implicit_write_only.v.

the right-hand expression shall be evaluated before the delay, instead of after the delay; a repeat count "less than or equal to 0 at the time of evaluation" means no wait. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/d04_05_intra_assignment_delay_blocking.v, d04_06_intra_assignment_event_blocking.v, d04_07_intra_assignment_delay_nonblocking.v, b_9_7_7_repeat_event_control.v (xfail).

The sequential block shall be delimited by the keywords begin and end. The procedural statements in sequential block shall be executed sequentially in the given order. and "The procedural statements in parallel block shall be executed concurrently." An introduction; the declaration rules are §9.8.1 to §9.8.3 (cited both ways). Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_8_1_sequential_block.v, b_9_8_4_parallel_block_timing.v.

Start and finish times, and "Execution shall not continue to the statement following a block until the finish time for the block has been reached". Nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_8_4_parallel_block_timing.v (Examples 1 and 2), d04_13_fork_join_is_concurrent.v.

The initial construct shall execute only once ... the always construct shall execute repeatedly. "There shall be no limit to the number of initial and always constructs". "There shall be no implied order of execution between initial and always constructs" is unspecified (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). Nothing is illegal (the null-statement ban is §9.9.1/§9.9.2's). Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/b_9_9_initial_and_always.v.
Tasks and functions provide the ability to execute common procedures from several different places in a description. The chapter preamble; its rules are in §10.1 to §10.4.5, each cited both ways.

column3: Task memory usage and concurrent activation
Disabling of named blocks and tasks

column4: The purpose of a function is to return a value that is to be used in an expression. The rest of this clause explains how to define and use functions. An introduction; the rules are §10.4.1 to §10.4.5, each cited both ways.

column3: Returning a value from a function

column4: The chapter heading; it states no rule of its own. Its rules are §11.1 to §11.6.7.
This clause gives an overview of the interactions between these elements, especially with respect to the scheduling and execution of events. An introduction; states no rule.

These resulting definitions provide the standard Verilog reference model for simulation, which all compliant simulators shall implement. ... "Every change in value of a net or variable ..., as well as the named event, is considered an update event." Definitions of the model; nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/b_11_2_update_events.v (a named event, a net change and a variable change wake their waiters; a write of the same value does not).

The five regions and their order: inactive after active, nonblocking assign updates after both, monitor events last; #0 makes the process an inactive event. An ordering, nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/b_11_3_region_order.v (two #0 resumptions before a pending NBA, $strobe after it), scheduling.v, 09_behavioral_modeling/d06_intra_assign_delay.v.

The reference algorithm (inactive, then nonblocking assign update, then monitor events are activated when no active event is left). An algorithm, nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/b_11_3_region_order.v.

Statements within a begin-end block shall be executed in the order in which they appear and "Nonblocking assignments shall be performed in the order the statements were executed". Guarantees; nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/scheduling.v, 09_behavioral_modeling/audit_nba_same_time_updates.v (two NBAs to one variable in one time step, both performed, in order).

active events can be taken off the queue and processed in any order and "At any time while evaluating a behavioral statement, the simulator may suspend execution" (statements without time control "do not have to be executed as one event"); the order is "nondeterministic and not under control of the user", so no test may assert one outcome (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). 11_scheduling/audit_sched_allowed_active_race.v asserts only membership in the permitted set; the audit_sched_*_order.v fixtures pin VerA's own order and say the LRM also accepts others.

The simulator is correct in displaying either a 1 or a 0. The clause's example race has two permitted outcomes, so no test may assert one (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). 11_scheduling/audit_sched_allowed_active_race.v is the example, asserting only that the value is one of the two.
Assignments are translated into processes and events as detailed in 11.6.1 through 11.6.7. An introduction; the rules are §11.6.1 to §11.6.7.

A continuous assignment process is also evaluated at time 0 to ensure that constant values are propagated. Event semantics; nothing is illegal (a continuous assignment to a variable is §6.1.2's ban). Positive: 11_scheduling/audit_sched_constant_ports.v, 06_assignments/d06_cont_assign_reeval.v.

An assign or force "corresponds to a process that is sensitive to the source elements in the expression" and "A deassign or a release statement deactivates any corresponding assign or force statement(s)." Event semantics; nothing is illegal (the target restrictions are §9.3.1's and §9.3.2's). Positive: 11_scheduling/b_11_6_2_procedural_continuous_tracks_sources.v.

The values at the time the process resumes are used to determine the target(s). Event semantics; nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/audit_sched_blocking_target_return.v, 09_behavioral_modeling/d04_05_intra_assignment_delay_blocking.v.

The values in effect when the update is placed on the event queue are used to compute both the right-hand value and the left-hand target. Event semantics; nothing is illegal. Positive: 09_behavioral_modeling/audit_nba_index_snapshot.v, d04_07_intra_assignment_delay_nonblocking.v.

Switch processing shall consider all the devices in a bidirectional switch-connected net before it can determine the appropriate value for any node on the net and the x-gate rule (a node with one level in every conducting/nonconducting combination takes it, any other x). Nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/b_11_6_5_switch_x_gate.v, 07_gate_switch_level/d08_bidirectional.v.
Task/function argument passing is by value, and it copies in on invocation and copies out on return. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 11_scheduling/audit_sched_task_copy_timing.v.

When the two nets connected by a port are of different net type, the resulting single net can be assigned one of the following. It types the single net of a merge, and §12.3.10 leaves merging to the tool ("It is permissible to merge the dominating and dominated nets into a single net"); merged and unmerged dissimilar nets resolve differently when both sides drive, so no test may assert the resolved type (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). Not optional: CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.2 is for language subsets a tool opts into, and nothing in the source selects merging. The merge-independent obligations, the warn cells, are §12.3.10's (12_hierarchy/b_12_3_10_net_type_warning.v, xfail).

The simulated net shall take the net type specified in the table and the delay specified for that net. The simulated net exists only when a tool merges, which §12.3.10 permits and does not require, so no test may assert its type or delay (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). The warn cells, owed either way, are pinned by 12_hierarchy/b_12_3_10_net_type_warning.v (xfail).

"It shall be typed, sized, and evaluated, and the resulting value assigned to the object on the other side of the port using the same rules as an assignment." Nothing is illegal. This clause describes system tasks and functions that are considered part of the Verilog HDL. These system tasks and functions are divided into ten categories A list of the tasks by category; the rules are in §17.1 to §17.11.

The display group of system tasks is divided into three categories: the display and write tasks, strobed monitoring tasks, and continuous monitoring tasks. An introduction; the rules are §17.1.1 to §17.1.3, each cited both ways.

Table 17-1 defines what each escape sequence displays; "If fewer than three characters are used, the following character shall not be an octal digit" is part of the definition (a following octal digit would be read as part of \ddd), and "Implementations may issue an error if the character represented is greater than \377" is optional. Nothing a tool must refuse. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_1_1_1_escape_sequences.v (the clause example and \ddd of one to three digits).

For expression arguments, the values written to the output file (or terminal) are sized automatically. ... "The automatic sizing of displayed data can be overridden by inserting a zero". Sizing rules; nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_display_decimal_states.v, audit_display_write_runs.v; b_17_1_1_3_zero_width_format.v (xfail: %0h, %0b, %0o keep leading zeros).

The x/z digit rules for %d, %h, %o and %b ("If all bits in a group are at the unknown value, a lowercase x is displayed for that digit" ...). Display rules; nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_1_1_4_unknown_digits.v (the clause three examples and the z rules), audit_display_decimal_states.v.

The %m format specifier does not accept an argument. Instead, it causes the display task to print the hierarchical name of the module, task, function, or named block that invokes the system task. %m consumes no argument (a following expression is an ordinary argument), so nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_display_named_scope.v.

column3: File input-output system tasks and functions
column4: The system tasks and functions for file-based operations are divided into the following categories A list; the rules are §17.2.1 to §17.2.9.

Files opened using file descriptors can be read from only if they were opened with either the r or r+ type values. The restriction binds the file, not the source: whether a descriptor was opened for reading is known only at run time, and §17.2.4.1 fixes the outcome of such a read ("If an error occurs reading from the file, then c is set to EOF (-1)"). No source construct is illegal. Table 17-7 also calls w+ and a+ "update", which this sentence contradicts; the fixtures read only through r and r+. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_4_read_needs_read_type.v (a "w" descriptor reads -1; "r+" and "r" read the byte).

column3: Reading a character at a time
column4: $fgetc reads a byte or returns EOF (-1) on error; $ungetc pushes a character back, returning 0 or EOF. Results defined for every input, errors reported by return value; nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_file_read_position.v, b_17_2_4_read_needs_read_type.v.

column3: Reading a line at a time
column4: reads characters from the file specified by fd into the reg str until str is filled, or a newline character is read and transferred to str, or an EOF condition is encountered ... "If an error occurs reading from the file, then code is set to zero." Results defined for every input; nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_4_2_fgets.v (xfail: $fgets is not implemented in the digital context).

$fread loads a reg or memory byte by byte, big endian, from start for at most count words; "If an error occurs reading from the file, then code is set to zero." Nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_4_4_fread.v (xfail: $fread is not implemented in the digital context).

$ftell, $fseek (operations 0, 1, 2), $rewind, the gap rule and append positioning; "If an error occurs repositioning the file, then code is set to -1." Errors are return values; nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_5_seek_gap_and_origin.v, audit_file_read_position.v; b_17_2_5_append_writes_at_end.v (xfail: an "a" file is overwritten after $fseek).

writes any buffered output to the file(s) specified by mcd, to the file specified by fd, or if $fflush is invoked with no arguments, to all open files. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_6_fflush.v (xfail: $fflush is not implemented in the digital context).

If the most recent operation did not result in an error, then the value returned shall be zero, and the reg str shall be cleared. The nonzero code of an error is not fixed ("an error code is returned"; CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5), so only zero/nonzero is asserted. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_2_7_ferror.v (xfail: $ferror is not implemented in the digital context).
returns a nonzero value when EOF has previously been detected reading the input file fd. It returns zero otherwise. Nothing is illegal. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_file_read_position.v.

The $stop system task causes simulation to be suspended. This task takes an optional expression argument (0, 1, or 2) that determines what type of diagnostic message is printed. The amount of diagnostic messages output increases with the value What a suspended simulation does next (an interactive prompt, reading input, how a batch run ends) and the text of each diagnostic level are the tool's, so no transcript is portable. VerA's analog choice is CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.3's print-and-exit-0 row; the digital runner refuses $stop (E1100 "not implemented"), a gap. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_pla_async_personality.v.

The logic arrays are modeled with and, or, nand, and nor logic planes. This applies to all array types and formats. Names the four planes; nothing is forbidden. Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_5_2_logic_planes.v (all four planes, array and plane formats).

This subclause describes a set of system tasks and functions that manage queues. All of the queue management tasks and functions return an output status code. Table 17-16 is how an invalid operation (undefined q_id, bad type, nonpositive length, duplicate q_id, full or empty queue) is reported at run time; none is illegal source. Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_queue_status_boundaries.v (codes 2, 4, 5, 6).

The following system functions provide access to current simulation time: $time $stime $realtime A list introducing §17.7.1 to §17.7.3, each cited both ways. Positive: 17_system_tasks/d09_05_time_queries.v, d09_06_time_rounding.v.

There is a set of random number generators that return integer values distributed according to standard probabilistic functions. An introduction; the rules are §17.9.1, §17.9.2 (cited both ways) and §17.9.3 (classified). Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_9_2_same_seed_same_value.v.

The algorithm for these functions is defined by the following C code The reference listing fixes every value; nothing is forbidden, and its inf/NaN and precision behaviour is unasserted (CLAUSE-AUDIT §5.5). Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_dist_reference.v, audit_random_seed_reference.v.

These arguments, referred to below as plusargs, are accessible through the system functions described in 17.10.1 and 17.10.2. An introduction; the rules are those two clauses (cited both ways). Positive: 17_system_tasks/b_17_10_1_plusargs_variable_query.v.

There are integer and real math functions. The math system functions may be used in constant expressions, as specified in Clause 5. Permissive; the argument rules are §17.11.1 and §17.11.2 (cited both ways). Positive: 17_system_tasks/audit_ieee_math_constant_expression.v, d09_10_clog2.v.
A VCD file contains information about value changes on selected variables in the design stored by VCD system tasks. Two types of VCD files exist The chapter preamble; its rules are in §18.1 to §18.4.

The steps involved in creating the four-state VCD file are listed below (insert the VCD system tasks, run the simulation) and "A VCD file is an ASCII file that contains header information, variable definitions, and the value changes for all variables specified in the task calls." A description of the flow; the tasks and their refusals are §18.1.1 to §18.1.6, each cited both ways. Positive: 18_vcd/d09_11_vcd_dumpvars.v, d09_12_vcd_dumpoff_on.v.

The dump file is structured in a free format. White space is used to separate commands and to make the file easily readable by a text editor. Binds the writer; no source construct can break it (the harness compares dumps as white-space separated tokens). Positive: 18_vcd/d09_11_vcd_dumpvars.v, d09_12_vcd_dumpoff_on.v.

Dumps of value changes to scalar variables shall not have any white space between the value and the identifier code. Dumps of value changes to vectors shall not have any white space between the base letter and the value digits, but they shall have one white space between the value digits and the identifier code. and Tables 18-1/18-2 shortening; events dump as scalars. Rules on the writer; nothing a design writes is illegal. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_2_table_18_2_shortening.v (every Table 18-2 row), d09_13_vcd_dumpvars_levels.v; b_18_2_2_event_marker.v (xfail: events are not dumped).

The general information in the VCD file is presented as a series of sections surrounded by keywords. Keyword commands provide a means of inserting information in the VCD file. Keyword commands can be inserted either by the dumper or manually. Table 18-3 lists them; each is its own subclause. Nothing is forbidden. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v.

The $comment section provides a means of inserting a comment in the VCD file. Syntax 18-9. Permissive; the one comment a writer must insert is the §18.1.5 limit notice. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_1_5_dumplimit_stops_with_comment.v (the $comment closing a limited dump).

The $date section indicates the date on which the VCD file was generated. Syntax 18-10. The date_text is the writer's and cannot be asserted; its presence can. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_8_version_names_dumpfile_literal.v (a non-empty $date section before $enddefinitions, read back).
The $enddefinitions section marks the end of the header information and definitions. Syntax 18-11. Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v.

The $scope section defines the scope of the variables being dumped. Syntax 18-12 scope_type begin | fork | function | module | task. Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v (nested module scopes); b_18_2_3_4_task_function_scopes.v (xfail: task and function scopes are not dumped).

The $timescale keyword specifies what timescale was used for the simulation. Syntax 18-13 time_number 1 | 10 | 100. Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v (`timescale 100ps/100ps -> $timescale 100ps).
The $upscope section indicates a change of scope to the next higher level in the design hierarchy. Syntax 18-14. Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v (two levels closed).

The $var section prints the names and identifier codes of the variables being dumped. Syntax 18-15, "Size specifies how many bits are in the variable", the msb/lsb reference, "a net of net type uwire shall have a variable type of wire". Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_7_var_sections.v (every net type, uwire as wire, reg, ascending range, integer, time); b_18_2_2_event_marker.v (xfail: no event $var).

The $version section indicates which version of the VCD writer was used to produce the VCD file and the $dumpfile system task used to create the file. If a variable or an expression was used to specify the filename within $dumpfile, the unevaluated variable or expression literal shall appear in the $version string. Binds the writer. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_3_8_version_names_dumpfile_literal.v; b_18_2_3_8_version_names_dumpfile_variable.v (xfail: the evaluated name is written).

The $dumpall keyword specifies current values of all variables dumped. A section the writer produces for the §18.1 task of the same name (whose refusals are §18.1.2 to §18.1.4). Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_4_example_value_changes.v.

The $dumpoff keyword indicates all variables dumped with X values. A section the writer produces for the §18.1 task of the same name (whose refusals are §18.1.2 to §18.1.4). Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_4_example_value_changes.v.

The $dumpon keyword indicates resumption of dumping and lists current values of all variables dumped. A section the writer produces for the §18.1 task of the same name (whose refusals are §18.1.2 to §18.1.4). Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_4_example_value_changes.v.

The section beginning with $dumpvars keyword lists initial values of all variables dumped. A section the writer produces for the §18.1 task of the same name (whose refusals are §18.1.2 to §18.1.4). Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_4_example_value_changes.v.

The following example illustrates the format of the four-state VCD file. An example of §18.2.1 to §18.2.3; nothing is forbidden. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_2_4_example_value_changes.v (the example's every value-change section, $dumpvars at #500 to #2010).

The four-state VCD file rules and syntax apply to the extended VCD file unless otherwise stated in this subclause. A description of the flow; the tasks and their refusals are §18.3.1 to §18.3.5, each cited both ways. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_4_2_dumpports_node_information.v (xfail: $dumpports is not implemented, E1100).

var_type The keyword port. No other keyword is allowed. size 1 or the port's index, codes "<" from zero "in the order found in the module declaration". The state characters for input (D U N Z d u), output (L H X T l h) and unknown-direction (0 1 ? F A a B b C c f) values. A table the writer follows. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_4_3_port_value_changes.v (D U N H X l f and 1) (xfail: $dumpports is not implemented, E1100).

Drivers are considered only in terms of primitives, continuous assignments, and procedural continuous assignments. and the three conflict rules (same value and strength range: 0/1 and the stronger strength; strong input over weak output: d/u; weak input under strong output: l/h). How the writer resolves a port; nothing is illegal. Positive: 18_vcd/b_18_4_3_port_value_changes.v (p1 0 6 and pl 6 0) (xfail: $dumpports is not implemented, E1100).
